title: Cycle 25: persistent server-side token-family store for local-auth
summary: Moved BrowserOS local-auth token families from an in-memory Map to a durable SQLite store. Refresh-token rotation now runs inside an immediate transaction, so concurrent /auth/refresh requests cannot both win. Only SHA-256 hashes are persisted. TriOS clients recover from server restart via /auth/refresh instead of bootstrap.
weak_spots: Token families were purely in-memory and lost on server restart
No administrative visibility into active families or rotation history
LocalAuthService.validate() could auto-issue a new family as a side effect
No atomic guard against concurrent refresh rotations
competitors: OWASP ASVS 5.0 V10 / RFC 9700 — server-side sessions as first-class objects
Postgres + Redis durable session store pattern
Atomic refresh rotation via SELECT FOR UPDATE or Redis Lua

variants.A: File-based JSON snapshot of families (simple, non-atomic)
variants.B: SQLite-backed family store with WAL + atomic rotation (implemented)
variants.C: Postgres-backed store with Redis cache (multi-instance, external deps)

lessons: Token-family store must persist hashes only and expose atomic rotation.
Validation must be read-only; never auto-issue a family inside validation.
SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes rotations; the second attempt sees reuse.
Clear is_active when revoking a family so getActiveFamily() never returns a revoked family.
Tests should use :memory: stores explicitly; default file paths are production-only.
Source-file-relative path math is fragile in monorepos; pass explicit paths derived from the server's configured executionDir and verify the runtime file location after launch.
